hints: Calculate the volume after 30 seconds: $V = 600 \times 30 = 18000\text{ cm}^3$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total volume of the spherical balloon after $30\text{ seconds}$ of pumping:
$$V = 600 \times 30 = 18000\text{ cm}^3$$

Use the volume formula for a sphere $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ to solve for radius $r$:
$$\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 18000 \implies r^3 = \frac{18000 \times 3}{4\pi} = \frac{13500}{\pi} \approx 4297.18$$
$$r = \sqrt[3]{4297.18} \approx 16.257 \approx 16.3\text{ cm} \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

hints: Use the chain rule $\frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{dV/dt}{dV/dr} = \frac{600}{4\pi r^2}$ with $r \approx 16.257$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the sphere volume formula with respect to radius $r$:
$$\frac{dV}{dr} = 4\pi r^2$$

Apply the chain rule for connected rates of change:
$$\frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{\frac{dV}{dt}}{\frac{dV}{dr}} = \frac{600}{4\pi r^2}$$
